races.title: State Senate, District 17
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mrs. Sydney Batch
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina Senate for District 17 since January 2021, appointed to fill a vacancy. Senate Democratic Leader since 2025. Earlier served in the state House (District 37, 2019–2021). Family law attorney, social worker and co-founder of a law firm.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed by Ballotpedia among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We could not confirm where she was born or raised or when she moved to North Carolina. One press quote on her campaign site calls her a "Triangle native," but we could not read the underlying article. We found no documented actions or stated positions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, immigration enforcement or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had.

qual.background: Served in the NC House (2019–2021) and NC Senate (2021–present), became Senate Minority Leader in 2025, and works as a family law attorney, social worker and law firm co-owner.
qual.why: Several years of legislative service plus chamber leadership as Senate Democratic Leader, combined with a legal career, fit the high band for writing law and the state budget.

cands.name: Shirley Johnson
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 17 in 2026. She won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary and lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Sydney Batch. No career or office history was found.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Shirley Johnson was born or raised, when she moved to North Carolina, or her work history, education, or any public offices held. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and no campaign website or platform statements were available. We found no documented positions on data centers, development, taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, education, or policing. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for her. We found no news coverage or controversies about her.
